title: UNIT TWO: PEOPLES AND CULTURES IN ETHIOPIA AND THE HORN
content:
ሰላም የEthioFresh ቤተሰቦች! 👋 እንኳን ወደ Unit 2 Tutorial በሰላም መጣችሁ! ይህ ኖት የዩኒቨርሲቲያችሁን ሞጁል መስመር በመስመር ተከትሎ፣ ለፈተና 100% ሙሉ በሙሉ እንድትዘጋጁና A+ እንድታስመዘግቡ በከፍተኛ ጥራት የተዘጋጀ የEthioFresh Tutorial ነው። በዚህ ክፍል የሰው ልጅ አመጣጥንና ታሪክን አብረን እናያለን👇! 🚀

2.1. Human Evolution

Human evolution accounts for only a fraction of the history of the globe, which evolved since circa/c. 4.5 billion years Before Present (BP).

Biological Timeline of Life on Earth:
• 4.5 Billion Years BP: Evolution of the Earth.
• 3 to 1 Billion Years BP: Emergence of the earliest primitive life forms.
• c. 800 Million Years BP: Emergence of blue-green algae, small plants, fishes, birds, and small organisms.
• 200–170 Million Years BP: Primates branched into placental mammals. Primates further differentiated into:
- Pongidae: Chimpanzee, gorilla, gibbon, orangutan, baboon, etc.
- Hominidae: Human ancestors.

Archaeological Fossils Discovered in Ethiopia and the Horn:
Archaeological evidence shows that the East African Rift Valley is the cradle of humanity. Key fossil discoveries include:
• Chororapithecus: Dated to 10 million BP; unearthed at Anchar in West Hararghe in 2007.
• Ardipithecus kadabba: Dated to 5.8–5.2 million BP; discovered in the Middle Awash.
• Ardipithecus ramidus: Dated to 4.2 million BP; discovered at Aramis in Afar in 1994.
• Australopithecines (Earlier Forms): Dated to 3.6 million BP; uncovered at Belohdelie in Middle Awash.
• Australopithecus afarensis (Selam): Fossil of a 3-year-old child dated to 3.3 million BP; discovered at Dikika, Mille in 2000.
• Australopithecus afarensis (Lucy/Dinkinesh): Dated to c. 3.18 million BP; discovered at Hadar in 1974 AD. She had 40% complete body parts, weighed 30 kg, stood 1.07 meters tall, and possessed a pelvis resembling that of a bipedal female.
• Australopithecus anamensis: Discovered around Lake Turkana in 1995.
• Australopithecus garhi: An eco-fact (literally meaning 'surprise' in the Afar language) dated to 2.5 million BP; discovered at Bouri in Middle Awash between 1996 and 1999.

The Genus Homo (Development of Human Brain & Genus Expansion):
The development of the human brain was the main feature of this stage, producing the genus Homo (emerged 2–2.5 million BP):
1. Homo habilis: Dated to 1.9 million BP; discovered in Lower Omo. Derived from Latin terms Homo (human being) and Habilis (skillful use of hands).
2. Homo erectus: Dated to 1.6 million BP; brain size of 900–1100 cc; means 'walking upright'. Discovered at Melka Kunture, Konso Gardula, and Gadeb. Originated in Africa and spread to the rest of the world.
3. Archaic Homo sapiens (Bodo): Dated to 400,000 BP; brain size of 1300–1400 cc; discovered in Middle Awash.
4. Homo sapiens sapiens: Sub-species dated to 100,000 BP; discovered at Porc Epic near Dire Dawa and Kibish around Lower Omo in 1967. Kibish fossils were re-dated in 2004 to 195,000 BP, representing the oldest date in the world for modern Homo sapiens.
5. Homo sapiens idaltu: Another sub-species found in Middle Awash in 1997; lived about 160,000 BP.

Cultural Evolution & Stone Age Technologies:
Cultural evolution is related to socio-economic transformations, conventionally grouped into the Stone, Bronze, and Iron Ages. Stone tools are classified into three modes:
• Mode I (Oldowan): Named after Olduvai Gorge, Tanzania. Characterized by crude and mono-facial styles produced by direct percussion (striking the stone directly).
• Mode II (Acheulean): Named after St. Acheul, France. Produced by indirect percussion using hand-axe or hammer; characterized by bifacial, pointed, and convex features.
• Mode III (Sangoon): Characterized by a flexible and refined production style using obsidian (a black glass-like volcanic rock).

Key Archaeological Sites for Tool Finds:
• Dikika (Afar): Fossilized animal bones dating back to 3.4 million BP with stone-tool-inflicted marks (oldest evidence of stone tool use in the world).
• Gona (2.52 million BP) & Shungura: Oldowan tools made by Homo habilis.
• Kella (1963) & Konso: Acheulean tools (aged over 1 million years) produced by Homo erectus. Homo erectus also invented fire and initiated burial practices.
• Gademotta (Rift Valley): Sangoon tools dated back to 200,000 BP made by Homo sapiens.
• Other Sites: Gorgora, Ki’one, Yabello in Ethiopia, and Midhidhishi and Gudgud in Somalia.

Sub-divisions of the Stone Age:
• Paleolithic (Old Stone Age, 3.4 million to 11,000 BP): Period when humans developed language, sheltered in caves, and used stone, bone, wood, fur, and skin for food/clothing preparation. Division of labor existed based on sex and age (able-bodied males hunted animals; children and females gathered plants).
• Mesolithic (Middle Stone Age, 11,000–10,000 BP): Transition period between Paleolithic and Neolithic Ages.

👉
የሰው ልጅ በባዮሎጂካል እና ባህላዊ እድገት ውስጥ ረጅም የዝግመተ ለውጥ (evolution) መንገዶችን አልፏል። ምስራቅ አፍሪካ፣ በተለይም የኢትዮጵያ የስምጥ ሸለቆ (East African Rift Valley) የሰው ልጅ መገኛ ወይም "Cradle of Humanity" በመባል ይታወቃል።
1. የቅሪተ አካላት (Fossils) ቅደም ተከተል:
- Chororapithecus (10 ሚሊዮን ዓመት BP) ⇒ አንቻር፣ ምዕራብ ሐረርጌ።
- Ardipithecus kadabba (5.8–5.2 ሚሊዮን BP) እና Ardipithecus ramidus (4.2 ሚሊዮን BP) ⇒ ማዕከላዊ አዋሽ (አፋር)።
- Lucy/Dinkinesh (3.18 ሚሊዮን BP) ⇒ በሐዳር የተገኘች፣ 40% ሙሉ አካል ያላት እና በሁለት እግሯ የምትሄድ (bipedal) ሴት ቅሪተ አካል።
- Selam (3.3 ሚሊዮን BP) ⇒ የ3 ዓመት ህፃን ቅሪተ አካል በዲኪካ።
- Australopithecus garhi (2.5 ሚሊዮን BP) ⇒ 'Garhi' ማለት በአፋርኛ "ድንቅ/ግርም" (surprise) ማለት ነው።
2. የ Homo ዘሮች እድገት:
- Homo habilis ⇒ Skillful use of hands (እጁን በጥሩ ሁኔታ የሚጠቀም)፣ የመጀመሪያውን የድንጋይ መሣሪያ (Oldowan) የሠራ።
- Homo erectus ⇒ Walking upright (ቀጥ ብሎ የሚሄድ)፣ እሳት ያመነጨ እና የቀብር ሥነ-ሥርዓት የጀመረ።
- Homo sapiens sapiens (Kibish) ⇒ በ195,000 BP የቀደመ የዘመናዊ ሰው መገኛ።
3. የድንጋይ መሣሪያዎች (Modes of Tools):
- Mode I (Oldowan): ድንጋይን በቀጥታ በመምታት የሚዘጋጅ (direct percussion)።
- Mode II (Acheulean): ባለሁለት ፊት (bifacial) መጥረቢያዎች።
- Mode III (Sangoon): ከእሳተ ገሞራ መስታወት (Obsidian) የሚሰራ የተራቀቀ መሳሪያ።

💡 Exam Hints:
• Oldest Evidence of Stone Tool Use: Found at Dikika (3.4 million BP).
• Oldest Modern Human (Homo sapiens sapiens): Kibish fossils re-dated to 195,000 BP.
• Fire & Burial Invention: Attribute to Homo erectus.
• Meaning of Garhi: Literally means "surprise" in the Afar language.

😂 ቀልድ ላፍታ: 'ድሮ Homo habilis' ድንጋይ ሲቀጠቅጥ 'I'm an engineer!' ብሎ ያስብ ነበር፤ እኛ ግን ዛሬ በፈተና ላይ የሱን ስም ለመያዝ እንጨነቃለን! 😜


2.2. Neolithic Revolution

During the Neolithic period (New Stone Age/10,000–6,000 BP), human beings transformed from a mobile to a sedentary way of life with a radical shift from hunting and gathering to the domestication of plants and animals.

Causes of Agriculture & Domestication:
• Climatic change and an increased population of hunters and gatherers resulted in a decline in animal numbers and plant availability.
• As food gatherers were already aware of the growth cycle of most grass types, they began cultivating common plants that yielded edible seeds.
• Over-hunting reduced big animals, encouraging the domestication of smaller, easily managed animals.

Plant & Animal Domestication in Ethiopia and the Horn:
• Indigenous Plants Cultivated: In elevated and wetter parts of the Horn, crops such as eragrotis teff (teff), dagussa (eleusine coracana), nug (guzotia), and ensete ventricosum (enseat) were cultivated.
• Animal Species: Nidamawa and Zebu (Bos indicus) cattle were domesticated and expanded throughout Ethiopia and the Horn.

Archaeological Material Evidence of Neolithic Culture:
• Emba-Fakeda (Adigrat, Tigray), Aqordat & Barentu (Eritrea): Polished axes, beads, ceramics, grinding stones, stone figures, and animal remains.
• Gobodara Rock Shelter (Aksum): Agricultural stone tools.
• Lalibela Cave (Lake Tana Shore): Remains of domesticated cattle, chickpeas, and vegetables.
• Laga Oda Rock Shelter (Chercher): Stone tools for cutting grass and rock paintings of tamed animals.
• Lake Basaqa (Matahara): Evidence of domesticated cattle.
• External Comparative Sites: Playa Napata and Kado (Sudan), Cyrenaica (Libya), and Futajalon (West Africa).

👉
Neolithic Revolution (የኒዮሊቲክ አብዮት) ማለት የሰው ልጅ ከቦታ ቦታ ከመዘዋወርና ከማደን/ሰብል ከመሰብሰብ (hunting and gathering) ተላቆ፣ በአንድ ቦታ በመቀመጥ እፅዋትን ማልማት (ግብርና) እና እንስሳትን ማላመድ (domestication) የጀመረበት ታላቅ የኑሮ ለውጥ ነው።
1. ሀገር በቀል የበቀሉ ሰብሎች: ጤፍ (eragrotis teff)፣ ዳጉሳ (dagussa)፣ ኑግ (nug) እና እንሰት (ensete ventricosum) በኢትዮጵያ ደጋማ ቦታዎች መኮትኮት ጀመሩ።
2. የቀንድ ከብቶች: ዛቡ (Zebu - Bos indicus) የተባሉ የከብት ዝርያዎች ተገሩ።
3. አስፈላጊ የመስክ ማስረጃዎች (Archaeological Sites):
- ላሊበላ ዋሻ (ጣና ሀይቅ): የቤት እንስሳት፣ ሽምብራ (chickpeas) እና የአትክልት ቅሪቶች።
- ለጋ ኦዳ (ጨርጨር): የቤት እንስሳት የድንጋይ ላይ ስዕሎች (rock paintings)።
- ጎቦደራ (አክሱም): የግብርና ድንጋይ መሣሪያዎች።
- ባሳቃ ሀይቅ (መታሃራ): የቤት እንስሳት አጥንት መረጃ።

💡 Exam Hints:
• Definition of Neolithic Revolution: Transition from mobile/hunting-gathering to sedentary agriculture and animal domestication.
• Scientific Name of Teff: Eragrotis teff.
• Rock Paintings of Tamed Animals Site: Laga Oda rock shelter in Chercher.
• Domesticated Chickpeas Evidence: Found at Lalibela Cave near Lake Tana.
